title: ALL THE FAT IS THE LORD'S

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'The priest shall burn them on the altar as a food offering, a pleasing aroma. All the fat is the LORD's.'" - Lev 3:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Four words close this instruction: all the fat is the LORD's.

Not some of it. Not a token portion representing the rest. All of it. The best of everything brought to that altar belonged to God by right, not by the worshipper's generosity.

This is a different way of thinking about giving than most of us are used to. We tend to imagine that everything is ours, and giving means transferring some of our property to God. Scripture consistently reverses that. The earth is the LORD's, and everything in it (Ps 24:1). David prayed, "Everything comes from you, and we have given you only what comes from your hand" (1 Chr 29:14).

So the fat was never really the Israelite's to keep. Bringing it was not generosity. It was honesty.

That reframes the whole question of what we give God. The issue is not how much of my life I am willing to hand over. It is how much of God's life in me I am willing to acknowledge. Paul asks the Corinthians, "What do you have that you did not receive?" (1 Cor 4:7).

Everything good in your hands today arrived there from somewhere. Give God the best of it, because it was always His.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I think of my possessions and abilities as mine, or as entrusted to me?
2. What would change if I approached giving as returning rather than sacrificing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, everything I hold came from You and belongs to You. Free me from the illusion of ownership and make me a faithful steward. Amen.
